title: Cascade attribution error — failure blamed on upstream task that actually succeeded
description: Task 5 in a composition chain fails. failure_mode classifier marks it as `cascading` from task 3 because task 3 was upstream. But task 3's output was correct; task 5 failed for an independent reason (resolver timeout, network blip, unrelated input). Posterior update penalizes task 3's variant; recommendation engine deprioritizes a working activity. This is the structural pair of FP-11 (silent semantic failure): there, success was wrong; here, failure attribution is wrong.

preconditions: failure_mode classifier marks downstream task as cascading from upstream
upstream task's output_impulse_ids appear correct under replay or shape/signature comparison to baseline

traces.synthesize: Build a composition A→B→C trace where A succeeds normally, B succeeds normally, C fails due to a deliberately-injected resolver timeout. failure_mode classifier (per FailureModeSchema heuristics) will mark C as cascading from B.

goal_text: Identify execution chains where a task is marked failure_mode='cascading' from an upstream task, but the upstream task's outputs are valid by independent witnesses (replay produces same outputs, downstream tasks in OTHER chains successfully consumed them). Propose an attribution-disambiguation activity that downgrades 'cascading' to 'independent_failure' in those cases and reverts the spurious Thompson penalty.

detection.signal: Trace C marked failure_mode.type='cascading' with context.upstream_task_id=T_B; but the same output_impulse_ids from T_B are successfully consumed by ≥ 1 other trace D within the next 24h with success=true.
detection.query_template: SELECT id, tasks FROM activity_execution_traces WHERE failure_mode.type = 'cascading' AND created_at > time::now() - 7d; CROSS-REFERENCE upstream output_impulse_ids with traces[*].input_impulse_ids WHERE success = true

recovery_test.regression_query: After reclassification activity ships, planted cascade-attribution scenario should result in upstream task's α being restored to pre-incident value (within tolerance) on the next harness run.

subagent_investigation.findings_summary: Cascade tag is assigned heuristically — IterationResolver defaults to type='cascading' for ANY sub-resolver error without checking upstream output validity. Posterior update: cascading victim gets {αΔ=0, βΔ=0}, but propagateCreditAlongChain applies β+=γ^1 to direct parent (depth-1). Result: spurious penalty on a working upstream variant. Traces are immutable; no failure_mode update path exists. Cross-trace witness query (input_impulse_ids overlap) is implementable on existing per-task impulse_ids but no query joins on it today.
code_references: repos/metabob-activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts:61-130 (per-task input/output impulse_ids extraction — usable for witness query)
current_gaps_in_codebase: No output-validity inspector on upstream task before cascade is recorded
No downstream-witness query that joins on input_impulse_ids
No mutable failure_mode revision endpoint (traces are append-only)
